thread:
Maya: heads-up — multiple tenants on dedicated-eu-west-1 started seeing 429s at ~2025-11-02T09:07Z. Symptoms: regen failures, elevated latency, and KV eviction storms.
Devon: adding eng-runtime + eng-infra. Any deploys or autoscale events?
Maya: no deploys. Autoscaler didn't add pods; throttle tripped. Snapshot: "kv_evictions_min=1620, kv_frag_pct=71, rss_mb=12120"
Suhas: 1620/min is a serious eviction wave. Do we see long-contexts from a single tenant or many tenants?
Maya: looks multi-tenant. Two high-volume customers hitting mixed workloads: many short chats plus sparse 5-6k regen loops. The mixed allocation sizes seem to shred arenas.
Emma: confirmed host family uses legacy arena allocator on this SKU — no compaction. That plus bimodal allocation sizes (small chat entries + large regen entries) causes fragmentation holes.
SupportBot: incident created INC-2025-4988 assigned to eng-runtime
Maya: customer repro snippet they ran (scaled):
```
# parallel mix: short and long
for s in range(60):
  post(short_prompt)
for s in range(20):
  post(long_6k_prompt)
```
Devon: can you paste per-worker kv hist + lru evict timeline? Also want per-tenant token-window and kv_entry_counts.
Maya: pasted (trimmed):
```
[09:06:54] w-4: kv_alloc_mb=8042 used_mb=7730 frag=64 evicts=420
[09:07:02] w-4: kv_alloc_mb=8042 used_mb=7986 frag=69 evicts=1140
[09:07:18] w-4: kv_alloc_mb=8042 used_mb=8028 frag=71 evicts=1620
[09:07:45] w-4: throttle_open=1 reason=kv_pressure
```
Suhas: fragmentation >70% with rapid evictions — allocator holes from alternating small/large entries. Multi-tenant churn means LRU can't reclaim contiguous regions easily.
Devon: can infra apply an emergency per-tenant kv_token_window and kv_entry_cap to stop blast behavior? We need a short circuit to stop cross-tenant cascade.
Emma: yes, can push control-plane limits. Propose: set kv_entry_cap=200000 for tenants A+B and kv_token_window=4096 for tenant B (who runs 6k by default).
Maya: applying now.
infra-console: config change applied by infra-console at 2025-11-02T09:12:03Z (kv_entry_cap set).
Maya: after limits, evict/min dropped to ~480, frag_pct to 62, errors falling.
Suhas: good stabilization. Root cause path: legacy allocator + mixed-size workloads + regen loops -> fragmentation -> evict cascade -> throttles. Need to confirm by repro with compaction enabled.
Devon: owners: Suhas (eng-runtime) will run staging experiment enabling compacting allocator flag; Emma (eng-infra) to coord control-plane caps and schedule any restarts; Maya to collect customer repro traces + billing spike. I'll prepare support KB.
Maya: customer ran scaled repro; logs uploaded: https://internal.redwood.ai/profiles/1764501234-multi-tenant-kv-repro
Suhas: experiment plan: run identical mix on staged dedicated worker with compacting allocator and a matched worker with legacy allocator; collect frag_pct, evict_rate, avg_kv_entry_size, and tail latency.
Emma: note: restarts required to enable compaction on that SKU. We'll drain one worker and flip flag. Minimal disruption planned. Schedule 1-min drain windows.
Devon: short-term mitigations for KB: 1) apply per-tenant kv_entry_cap and token window; 2) route regen-heavy tenants to variants with smaller KV footprints; 3) ask customers to use streaming/regenerative patterns that reuse prefixes when possible; 4) enable eviction backoffs for high-frag hosts.
Maya: also flag billing: large regen loops created token billing spike; customer wants refund review. Attached billing window.
Suhas: if compacting allocator reduces frag_pct by >25% and evict_rate by >40% under same load, recommend rollout path: staged deploy -> gradual rollout -> enable telemetry for avg_kv_entry_size and tenant_frag_pct alert.
Emma: implemented new alert: frag_pct > 65% AND evict_rate > 500 -> page eng-runtime. Dashboards updated.
Maya: customers are stable now; we'll keep caps for 48h while experiments run.
Devon: please drop heap+kv profiles here when ready. I'll update INC-2025-4988 and draft follow-up RFC for allocator upgrade.
SupportBot: INC-2025-4988 updated with actions and links.
Maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Devon: nice triage — keeping caps until runtime confirms fix.
